title: Wattlab: charging speed test for Android
description: Wattlab measures the real watts going into your battery, tells you why a charge is slow, and ranks your chargers and cables with a 60-second test. Free on Google Play.
og_title: Wattlab: is it the charger, the cable or the phone?
og_description: Real charging watts, the reason a charge is slow, and a 60-second test that ranks your chargers and cables. Free on Google Play.
ld_description: Charging speed test that measures the power going into the battery, explains slow charging, and ranks chargers and cables.
h1: Is it the charger, the cable or the phone?
lede: Wattlab measures the power actually going into your battery, tells you why a charge is slow, and ranks your chargers and cables with a 60-second test you can repeat.
free_note: Free. Pro is a one-time purchase, not a subscription.
bench_title: One phone, four ways to charge it

notes.original: A 90 W charger showing about 30 W is normal: phones cut fast charging as they fill.
notes.small: A smaller charger on the same cable: less than a third of the speed.
notes.generic: The same 90 W charger on a generic cable: about a twentieth of the speed.
notes.computer: A computer's USB port is the slowest of the four.

bench_note: Results of Wattlab's 60-second test on one phone, which its maker rates at up to 90 W.

shot.charge_alt: Wattlab's Charge screen: 30 W going into the battery, rated Fast, with 7,140 mA, 4.21 V, 32.4 °C and 47 minutes to full
shot.charge_title: How fast is it charging right now?
shot.charge_body: Live watts, current, voltage, temperature and time to full, calibrated for the way your phone reports them.
shot.slow_alt: The Charge screen with a generic cable: 2.5 W, rated Slow, with the reason: Charging at basic USB speed
shot.slow_body: A speed verdict with the main reason: heat, a cable or port at basic USB speed, a nearly full battery, battery protection, wireless charging, or the phone's own top speed.
shot.result_alt: A test result: 31 W on average, rated Fast, the fastest result on this phone so far, with a 31 W peak and steady power
shot.result_title: Which charger and cable are fastest?
shot.result_body: A 60-second test gives average and peak watts and stability. Only tests started at a similar battery level are ranked together, so the comparison is fair.

screens_note: The speed test is free and unlimited. Screens show readings recorded on one phone.
health_title: Battery health, with its error range.
health_body: Leave a charge plugged in until it finishes, such as overnight, and Wattlab reads your battery's full capacity. It shows how far the charges disagree and how many it rests on, and a health percentage only when the design capacity is known.
cap_caption: A capacity estimate of {cap_value} mAh, plus or minus 3%, a range from {cap_low} to {cap_high} mAh. It rests on {cap_count} charges that read within 20 mAh of each other. The maker's rated capacity is {cap_rated} mAh, so battery health is about {cap_percent}%.
also_title: It keeps working after the test.

also.record_body: Turn on auto-record and each charge is logged in the background, from plug-in to unplug.
also.usage_body: How much battery you have used since unplugging, with screen-on and screen-off time shown apart, and a standby drain check.
also.alert_body: A notification at 80%, or at any level you pick from 50% to 100%.
also.widget_body: Charging watts and battery level, without opening the app.

nots: It can't make charging faster or repair a battery, and it doesn't claim to.
No cleaner, no charging animations, no lock-screen overlays.
No made-up numbers. A value your phone doesn't report is shown as not reported.
No account and no cloud sync. Readings and charge history stay on your phone.
honest_body: Phones report battery current in different units and signs. Wattlab checks how yours reports it before it shows a reading. Usage statistics send rounded ranges, never raw readings.
pro_body: Pro is a one-time purchase, not a subscription. It removes ads and adds full charge history with power and temperature curves, 7-day battery usage, battery health trends, charging habit reports, unlimited setups, an overheating alert and CSV export. Or watch an optional ad to open history, curves and reports for 24 hours.

cooldown.what: See your battery temperature, get an alert when your phone overheats, and find out what is heating it up.
